gauntlet.intent: roe-asymmetric-per-side (T4 domain-split variant): BLUE runs an ASW/AAW multi-mission screen under a single fleet-wide WeaponsTight flag, but the underlying doctrinal posture is intentionally asymmetric BY DOMAIN within the same side, not just by side as in gauntlet-forge-20260727-1455-t2-c3's flat BLUE-tight/RED-free split. BLUE's ASW thread (ka-27m-helix-a dipping-sonar helo + p-3c-orion-update-iii-2023 sonobuoy MPA screening for RED's pl-877-kilo-paltus-1992 SSK and pla-885-severodvinsk-yasen SSGN) is genuinely ID-required: submarine contacts are held at low basePd (0.30-0.35) representing unconfirmed/unclassified tracks that must be positively identified before becoming engageable, consistent with real-world submarine engagement caution against friendly-fire and collateral risk in a contested undersea environment. BLUE's AAW thread (eurofighter-typhoon + jas-39e-gripen-ng-2021 intercepting su-27sm-sm3-flanker-j-2013 + mig-29-fulcrum-c-1999) is modeled as confidently-tracked (basePd 1.0, full fire-control lock, no ID ambiguity) -- i.e. doctrinally BLUE intends a freer AAW posture even while running tight ASW caution. RED (opposingRoe WeaponsFree, corvettes mrk-shkval-pr-22800-karakurt + pk-368-vasily-bykov-pr-22160 escorting the sub threats) has no such restraint on either domain. SCHEMA CONSTRAINT NOTE: the policy schema exposes only one friendlyRoe/opposingRoe pair per scenario (verified against gauntlet-forge-20260727-1455-t2-c3 and the top-level fields available) -- there is no per-domain ROE field. This candidate therefore sets friendlyRoe=WeaponsTight fleet-wide for BLUE (the more conservative of the two intended domain postures) and expresses the intended ASW-tight/AAW-free domain split NARRATIVELY via this intent/oracle text and via the basePd asymmetry between the ASW detection entries (0.30-0.35, unconfirmed/held-for-ID) and the AAW detection entries (1.0, confident lock). In actual sim execution the single WeaponsTight flag will uniformly gate BLUE's AAW engagements too, even though doctrine intends them free -- this is a known, honestly-flagged simulation-vs-schema gap for this candidate, not a hidden assumption.
gauntlet.oracle: BLUE's ASW contacts never convert to genuine engageable tracks regardless of ROE, because basePd 0.30-0.35 keeps them below the threshold the detection pipeline typically needs for a firm fire-control track -- these are intentionally-unconfirmed contacts consistent with ID-required submarine engagement caution, expected to show as low-Pd non-detections or, if a track does form, as WeaponsTight denials. BLUE's AAW contacts (basePd 1.0, full lock) will still be blocked from firing by the fleet-wide WeaponsTight gate (RoeLevel.WeaponsTight always denies) despite the doctrinal intent to run AAW free -- expect these to register as denied engagements (ROE_WEAPONS_TIGHT) rather than the freely-converting kills an AAW-only-free narrative would otherwise predict, empirically illustrating the schema's single-ROE-per-side limitation. RED, WeaponsFree throughout with no domain restriction, is expected to convert some of its high-Pd air-domain and passive-sonar detections of BLUE into real kills across the tier-4 24-tick budget, while BLUE accumulates a real minDenials floor primarily from its AAW thread (the ASW thread more likely surfaces as absent/unconfirmed tracks than logged denials -- see t2-c3's expectProvenance note on EngagementAbortReason vs DecisionLog.PolicyDenials for the same accounting caveat, which applies here too).
